chunks: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged that the wergild (blood money) is inherited by the inheritors, except for the brothers from the mother, for they do not inherit anything from the wergild.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Wergild or blood money compensation paid to the heirs of a victim

ai.seo_question: Who inherits blood money and who is excluded according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the general heirs of the deceased inherit the blood money (diyah), brothers from the mother are specifically excluded from this share. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of maternal siblings in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing their inheritance rights in compensation for homicide from those of full or paternal brothers, thereby refining the application of Quranic inheritance principles to specific cases of homicide.
